label: GitHub
description: PR commands in M-p, the PRs view, PR numbers and merge states in tabs and Reopen's worktrees; off, the workspace asks GitHub nothing by itself (programs you run, such as codex-review and wtpr, still do)

label: Linear
description: Ticket commands in M-p, ticket titles in tab names and tickets in M-j's picker; off, the workspace asks Linear nothing by itself (programs you run, such as wt and worktree-done, still do)

label: Choose a ticket when none is found
description: M-i, in a tab with no ticket found, lists your Linear tickets and projects to choose its ticket from; off, M-i says the tab has no ticket, and M-p's "Choose this tab's ticket or project…" still lists them

label: Cache PR and ticket images
description: Keeps the pictures, stylesheet, scripts and drawn pages of the PR and ticket image views on this computer, up to 300 MB, so one opened again shows at once; off, everything is fetched and drawn each time, and the pictures are left out, since the page loads a picture only from a copy on this computer

label: Push notifications
description: A desktop notification, named for the tab, when a Claude tab waits on you

label: Finished tabs clear
description: When a tab's finished mark goes: once you look at the tab, or only when you next prompt it

label: Sidebar
description: The sidebar on the left of every window; M-s still hides or shows it for now

label: A tab whose diff finishes loading needs you
description: A tab you left while its diff (M-d) was telling its story goes under Needs you, saying Diff ready, with a notification, once the story is told or has failed, until you go back to it; a tab in front is left alone. Off, nothing marks the tab

label: Shade the sidebar
description: The sidebar is drawn on a shade of its own, a step darker than the panes, as UX 2.0's canvas draws it; off, it is drawn on the terminal's background as before. The chosen row keeps its shade and accent bar either way

label: Half-page scrolling
description: C-d and C-u in the sidebar, and the wheel over it, scroll its list half a screen down or up, the cursor moving with it, as in Vim, one flick of the wheel moving once; off, C-d and C-u run in the chosen tab as other Ctrl keys do and the wheel moves a tab at a time

label: Up and down wrap around
description: In the sidebar, j, k, the arrows, C-n and C-p go round from the last row to the first and from the first to the last, the notifications included; off, they stop at the list's ends. g, G and the wheel go to an end and stay either way

label: Set a tab's status by hand
description: Set its status… in a tab's menu, and M-p's Set this tab's status…, file the tab under the group you choose in the sidebar and mission control, marked set by you, until Switchboard's own reading of the tab changes, which takes it back; a pin and a reminder still win. Off, the choices are gone and any status you set is dropped

label: Sidebar repository filter
description: M-p's Filter the sidebar to a repository moves every other repository's tabs to an Other repos group at the bottom of the sidebar and mission control's Tabs view, whatever they are doing, until Show every repository's tabs clears it; the filter is kept across restarts. Off, the commands are gone and every tab is in its own group

label: Enter opens the row's menu
description: Enter or Space on a row of the sidebar opens the menu m opens for it, as Enter does in mission control: a tab's with Go to tab chosen for Enter and Peek chosen for Space, so a second press does what the key did alone; a notification's its own menu. l and the right arrow still go to the tab. Off, Enter goes to the tab or into the notification, and Space peeks at the tab, as before

label: Select several tabs
description: v in the sidebar, or a Shift-click on a tab, selects several tabs to close at once from one menu. Off, v does nothing, a Shift-click on a tab goes there as a click does, and the sidebar acts on one tab at a time

label: Resize the sidebar by dragging or the pane resize keys
description: A drag of the sidebar's right edge, or the pane resize keys (C-M-S-h and C-M-S-l) while it has the keys, gives it a width of its own, from 24 columns to half the window, kept through restarts; mission control's list of views in its place takes the same width and the same edge. "Use the default width" in the sidebar's own menu, and M-p's "Use the sidebar's default width", go back to sidebar.json's width. Off, the sidebar keeps its fixed width, its edge takes no drag and the pane resize keys move the pane's divider as they did before, a width kept left for when it is on again

label: Reminders in the sidebar
description: Tabs waiting on a reminder sit under Reminders in the sidebar. Off, they are left out of the sidebar, the top line counts them (⏰ 3) and a click there opens mission control's Reminders view; a tab comes back under Needs you when its reminder comes due

label: Build failing
description: A Build failing group in the sidebar and mission control for the tabs whose open PR has a failing check, asked of GitHub every minute, an idle one wearing a red ✗; off, they stay in Working or Idle with the failing count in their words #github

label: Show the landing queue
description: Tabs landing on the default branch with queue-and-clean, or waiting their turn, get a Landing group in the sidebar and mission control, in the landing queue's order, which a waiting tab's menu changes; off, they show as Working, and the queue still orders the landings

label: Land PRs through Switchboard's merge queue
description: In a repository that lands through PRs with no merge queue of GitHub's, and whose CI runs on a push to ci/train-* branches, queue-and-clean adds a PR whose checks passed to Switchboard's own queue, which tests up to four together on a ci/train branch and squash-merges them in order once its CI passes, so no PR has to be brought up to date with the default branch first; off, queue-and-clean turns on GitHub's auto-merge for each PR, and what is queued waits

label: Remove landed worktrees
description: Removes a worktree under a repository's .claude/worktrees once everything on its branch is on the default branch, nothing in it is uncommitted, nothing git ignores in it is of its own (tool output and caches, links and copies of the main clone's files go with it), no tab has it open and git hasn't changed its index or HEAD for an hour (a commit, a checkout, a staged file; a read such as git log doesn't count): when a tab in it closes, and hourly for each repository a tab has been in, after fetching the default branch. Its branch is kept, and a message names what went. Off, worktrees stay until you remove them, as Reopen's menu still does

label: Remove finished PR review checkouts
description: Removes the checkout of someone else's PR made for review (wtpr --untrusted, M-p's Review a contributor's PR, in ~/.cache/switchboard/pr-review) once its PR is merged or closed (asked of GitHub while Settings' GitHub is on) or it has gone 14 days unused (no tab in it, and wtpr not run on it again), and only when no tab has it open, no switchboard try runs on it and nothing in it is uncommitted or untracked: hourly and when a tab in one closes, never while you're away. Its try's home and its pr-review branch go with it, and a message counts what went and its size. Off, they stay until you remove them

label: Target branches follow the default branch
description: When a landing pushes to the default branch while autopilot or hand-started items land on another branch, opens a tab in the background that merges the default branch into that branch under its landing lock, runs the repository's tests and pushes it, so the branch and the builds made from it carry the default branch's work; a conflict or failing tests leave the merge in its worktree for you, marked red in the Landing view. Off, a target branch takes the default branch's work only when you merge it yourself; M-p's 'Bring a target branch up to date with the default branch' still runs it by hand

label: Watch the default branch's CI
description: While autopilot works on a repository, or a tab waits to land on it, and its landings test in CI, Switchboard looks at its default branch's CI every two minutes and tells you when it fails, naming the commit and the line of the log that says why. Off, nothing looks, and you hear of a failing default branch only from the next landing

label: Keep the computer awake while tabs work
description: While a tab's Claude works (background work and watches too, not a /loop between its runs) or autopilot, on and not paused, has tabs open, the computer doesn't sleep when idle (caffeinate on macOS, a logind inhibitor on Linux), shown by a ☕ at the top of the sidebar; it lets go two minutes after everything is idle, the display still sleeps, and a laptop closed with no display on it sleeps anyway. M-p's 'Keep the computer awake until I say' holds it whatever runs. Off, the computer sleeps on its own schedule unless held from M-p

label: Notifications
description: The Notifications block at the bottom of the sidebar: new Slack messages and your Linear inbox, which a click opens in mission control

label: PR notifications
description: The sidebar tells you when one of your PRs merges, is approved or its checks start failing, from the PRs board's lookups; off, it doesn't

label: M-a goes to notifications
description: M-a's walk of what needs you ends at the notifications while there are any, after the tabs, opening them as the sidebar's n does

label: M-a visits Build failing tabs
description: M-a's walk of what needs you goes on to the tabs under Build failing after those under Needs you, before the notifications; off, it passes them by

label: Notifications window
description: Moving the sidebar's cursor onto a notification, or clicking one, brings the Notifications window to the front as moving onto a tab does: a tab of its own listing every one with its whole message, Enter opening its menu and Esc going back, which M-p's "Go to the notifications" brings to the front too; off, Enter or a click on one in the sidebar does what it leads to

label: New notes
description: In the sidebar's notifications, a note written for you (a meeting's from Fathom, the standup) until you read it, Enter offering to open it in Notes

label: Next meeting
description: In the sidebar's notifications, from five minutes before a meeting until ten after it starts: its name, the tickets and PRs it mentions, and Enter or a click to join its call

label: Docs in the link view
description: The link view reads a Notion page or a Google Doc or Slides deck through Claude's connectors, a headless Haiku fetching it; off, they are read as any other page, which a private one won't let it

label: Chrome profiles
description: Links Switchboard opens (mission control, the link view, M-r, M-l, switchboard open-url) open in the Chrome profile browser.json gives their site, else its default profile; off, every link opens in the default browser

label: Standup note
description: Each weekday from 6am, a note in Standups written from the last working day: the PRs you merged, opened, worked on and reviewed, your tickets that changed state and your commits, then what is in progress today and the reviews waiting on you

label: Standup summary
description: Over the standup note's list of the last working day, two or three sentences summing it up, written by Claude (Haiku, no tools) from the PR, ticket and commit titles in that list

label: Today's todo note
description: Whether the Today's todo note starter routine is made running when this version first sets up the routines (it sends your notes' unticked items to Claude); after that, pause or resume it in mission control's Routines view. Kept off by default for a workspace still running an older Switchboard, which reads this list

label: Todo note time
description: The hour the Today's todo note starter routine runs at each day, when this version first sets up the routines; after that, change its schedule in mission control's Routines view. Kept for a workspace still running an older Switchboard, which reads this list

label: Meeting notes
description: Whether the Meeting notes starter routine is made running when this version first sets up the routines (once Fathom has worked); after that, pause or resume it in mission control's Routines view. Kept for a workspace still running an older Switchboard, which reads this list

label: Search everything
description: M-S-f opens a box that searches, with a chip to turn each source on or off, and lists the open tabs that name or show it and what your notes, Linear, GitHub and Slack hold for it, each read beside the pane with Enter, a tab gone to

label: Arrow keys reach the search chips
description: In M-S-f's box, Down goes from the field to the chips and on to the results, Up back the same way, and Left and Right move along the chips; off, Up and Down move through the results alone and Tab reaches the chips

label: Preview the chosen search result
description: M-S-f's box is wider and shows the chosen result beside the results (under them in a narrow box): where it was found and the lines around the match, the match's line lit; J and K scroll it with the results focused; off, the box lists the results alone

label: Slack in search everything
description: M-S-f searches Slack too, through your own Slack sign-in while "Read Slack through your own token" is on, else through Claude's connector, a headless Haiku making that one call, its results arriving a few seconds after the others

label: Files in reading order
description: M-d lists the changed files flat, documentation first and tests last, with Haiku ordering the code from most abstract to most concrete; off, flat, A to Z

label: Diff told as a story
description: M-d's file list grouped into a few pages Claude names from the whole diff (Haiku, or Sonnet for a large change, as "Model that tells the diff's story" picks) and the commits' messages, each with a heading, two or three sentences that make the case for it to the colleagues reviewing it, and a line of what to watch for, read from the change's core to its edges, and told in chapters (]c and [c move between them, yS copies the story as Markdown); off, the files keep the reading order by kind. Sends the diff's text and the commit messages, not only the paths, to Claude

label: Click in menus
description: A click takes an option of mission control's menus, Yes or No of a question or a numbered answer, and a click outside the box closes it; a right click on an item in mission control, the Notifications window or the sidebar opens its menu, and where no item is the view's (the sidebar's own in the sidebar); and a click picks an option of the PR view's, the update box's and M-w's menus; off, they take keys alone

label: Notifications hand off to a tab
description: Every notification's menu, and the Slack, Inbox, Calendar and Autopilot views' and a failing default branch's in the CI view, offers Send it to a tab, which pastes its words and link into the Claude of a tab you pick and sends them (Paste it into a tab, beside it, without sending), and Open a tab for it, which starts a tab with Claude told about it (a failing default branch's in its repository's main clone, told to fix it). Off, the menus keep their own choices only

label: Send it to a tab submits it
description: An item's Send it to a tab pastes its words and link into the Claude of the tab you pick and presses Enter, so that Claude starts on it; Paste it into a tab, beside it, pastes them without sending, to add to first. Off, Send it to a tab pastes without sending and Paste it into a tab isn't offered

label: Notifications show in their view
description: A notification whose kind a view lists (Slack, Inbox, Calendar, PRs, CI, Routines) leads its menu with Show it in the <view> view, which a click or Enter takes: mission control opens on that view with the cursor on its item. Off, its menu starts with its view's own first choice, such as Open it in Slack

label: Open boxes by the click
description: A menu or question a click opens appears beside the place clicked, so its options are a short move away; one opened by a key stays in the middle. Off, every box opens in the middle of the screen

label: Tab moves focus
description: Tab and Shift-Tab move a highlight through what can be clicked, as on a webpage, and Enter presses it (Space too, but in the sidebar, where Space peeks): in mission control the views' names, the filter, each section of the view (its rows reached with j and k) and the panes beside it, wrapping round, with [ ] switching views; in the sidebar each of its rows, M-Space opening mission control; and the options of every box and menu; off, Tab switches views in mission control and opens it from the sidebar

label: Show views as the list moves
description: Moving the cursor through mission control's list of views with j, k or the arrows brings each view to the front as it lands on it, the list keeping the keys; Enter then moves into the view, a view joins back and forward's trail once the cursor rests on it a second, and the list is one Tab stop, Tab going into the view in front and Shift-Tab back. Off, j and k only move the cursor, Enter opens the view, and Tab stops on each view's row

label: Highlight on hover
description: What a click would press lights under the mouse: in mission control the views' names, the filter, the cards and rows, a menu's options, Yes and No, an answer's options and easy mode's ×; the sidebar's tabs and notifications; the options of the PR view's, the update box's and M-w's menus; and the buttons of Notes' toolbar, its boxes' × and M-d's diff. In Ghostty and kitty the mouse pointer also turns into a hand over what a click presses (the workspace's sidebar, header, mission control and boxes, and in M-d's diff its buttons, its list's rows, the story map's chapters, a fold and a path:line in an answer) and a resizing arrow over a line between panes. Off, nothing follows the mouse and the pointer is never changed. Takes effect at once in mission control and the sidebar, and when a menu, Notes or the diff next opens

label: Keep the tabs sidebar in mission control
description: Mission control keeps the tabs sidebar and lists its groups and views in a column of its own beside it, the view to its right; off, while mission control is open the sidebar itself lists its groups and views, the tabs coming back as it closes

label: Pause lookups while away
description: Stop asking GitHub, Linear and the calendar for mission control's views, and telling the diff's stories ahead, while no terminal is attached, or the computer has been locked, or idle 10 minutes, with no key pressed in Switchboard since (from another computer over SSH too), and catch up on return

label: Look often
description: Ask GitHub and Linear every 15 seconds (the PR board every 30) and look at the Slack Home tab every 10, in place of every one or two minutes: about eight times as many requests, which can reach GitHub's 5,000 an hour

label: Notifications' history
description: Mission control's Notifications view keeps every notification of the last two weeks by day, with what each led to and whether the sidebar still shows it, in ~/.local/state/switchboard/notifications on this computer; off, the view shows only the sidebar's notifications, as they are now, and nothing is kept

label: Summaries of each turn
description: Each card says what its tab's last turn did, in a sentence Haiku writes as the turn ends from the turn's prompt and last reply, which this sends to Claude; off, as it is by default, nothing is sent and a card shows the reply's first line

label: Calendar
description: Mission control's Calendar view: today from the day /today last saved

label: RSVP from the Calendar
description: Answer an invitation yes, maybe or no from its Enter menu in the Calendar view, through Claude's Google Calendar connector

label: Attendees' photos in the Calendar
description: Show the photos of who is going to the Calendar view's chosen event, looked up by each attendee's email address in Linear and the Slack relay's app (users:read.email), which sends those addresses to them. Off, as it is by default, no address is sent and each attendee is their initial

label: Reminders
description: M-p's Remind me about this tab: the tab waits under Reminders with the time left, then moves to Needs you with a banner when it comes due, and mission control's Reminders view shows every tab's reminder on a month; off, reminders are neither set nor shown, and the view is gone

label: Slack
description: Mission control's Slack view: your mentions, DMs, thread replies and chosen channels from the last day, as /slack-updates saved them

label: Draw emoji in Slack messages
description: Slack's emoji show as emoji in the Slack view, its notifications and the reply box, and a workspace's own emoji as small pictures in the view's list and thread where the terminal draws images, which your own Slack sign-in (with the emoji:read scope) reads from Slack's emoji list and keeps on this computer for a week; off, emoji show as their codes, :thumbsup:, and no emoji is looked up

label: Slack without a tab
description: Mission control looks at Slack itself, as often as "Check Slack for new messages every" says, through your own Slack sign-in while "Read Slack through your own token" is on, else through cheap headless Haiku calls, instead of the Slack routine following the slack-updates skill

label: Check Slack for new messages every
description: How often mission control looks at Slack for new messages while you're at the computer and "Slack without a tab" is on. A look through Claude's connector rather than your own token goes out at most once a minute, since each is a model call; when Slack answers that its rate limit is spent, the look waits as long as Slack asks and then looks half as often for its next ten looks

label: Slack threads and pictures
description: The Slack view shows the chosen message's whole thread beside it, with its pictures and videos, which each look reads through your own Slack sign-in while "Read Slack through your own token" is on, else through Claude's Slack connector (a few more headless Haiku calls a look), and keeps on this computer; off, the view lists the messages alone and reads no threads or files

label: Reply from the Slack view
description: A Slack message's Enter menu in the Slack view offers to reply in its thread or its channel, or in its DM: a box to type in, and Send leaves your words as typed, through Claude's Slack connector, as Slack messages go out as says: a draft in Slack for you to send there, or sent at once after asking, naming who can read it. Off, as it is by default since it sends your words to Slack, the menu offers no replies

label: Slack messages go out as
description: How a message Switchboard sends as you leaves, the Slack view's reply among them: a draft in Slack, made in the conversation's composer through Claude's Slack connector with nothing asked first, the conversation then opened in Slack for you to send it there, since a message the connector sends carries a Sent using Claude line that Slack adds and a draft you send carries none; sent at once, after a question naming who can read it, with that line

label: Slack reminders in the Slack view
description: With a Slack sign-in of your own (switchboard setup slack-user), the Slack view lists your Slack reminders that are due under Reminders, read from Slack every two minutes while you're here, with their notifications among the view's; a reminder's menu marks it complete in Slack after asking. Without a sign-in the view says how to make one. Off, no reminders are read or listed

label: Mark what you open read in Slack
description: With a Slack sign-in of your own (switchboard setup slack-user), a message whose thread you open in the Slack view (Enter on it, or its thread shown for two seconds) is marked read in Slack up to it, unless you have read further there. Off, as it is by default since it changes what Slack shows you as unread, opening a message marks it seen only here

label: Read Slack through your own token
description: With a Slack sign-in of your own (switchboard setup slack-user), the Slack view's look, its threads and pictures, and search everything's Slack results read Slack's Web API with your token rather than a Claude connector call each, falling back to the connector when Slack refuses the token or a scope is missing, and saying why under the view's header. Off, every read goes through the connector

label: Reopen
description: Mission control's Reopen view: tabs closed and past Claude sessions to resume, with the last screen of each, and the worktrees no tab has open; off, M-o opens it still and nothing else lists them

label: PR board
description: Mission control's PRs view, which asks GitHub about your pull requests every two minutes

label: CI
description: Mission control's CI view: your pull requests failing, running and passing, each failed check with the line of its log that says why and its failing step beside the list, asked of GitHub every two minutes #github

label: Landing view
description: While a tab is landing or waiting to land, mission control shows each repository's landing queue or merge queue (everyone's PRs in it, asked of GitHub every 15 seconds), in queue order, with the tab that has each; a waiting one's menu moves it or takes it out

label: Autopilot view
description: While autopilot works a note, mission control shows a view of it: the note, its tabs working and open against its slots and cap, today's spend against its limit, and a board of every item it works, a card in the column where it stands (Next up, Blocked while an item waits on another, Working, Waiting on you, Landing, Landed, and Skipped while an item is skipped). Off, its line above the tabs stays and the view goes; on, the view takes the line's place

label: Autopilot
description: With it on, M-p's 'Autopilot: work a note' keeps tabs working through a note's checklist, opening the next item with wt as each lands; the mode itself starts off until you turn it on there. Off, it opens no tabs, and its line in mission control and its notification go

label: Close a worked note's landed tabs
description: When a tab autopilot opened closes once queue-and-clean has landed it and moved it back to the main clone: when seen, as soon as you leave it after seeing it, or 30 minutes after landing if you never look; at once, as soon as it lands; after 5 minutes, or sooner once seen and left; never, left open for you to close. Whatever the choice, a tab in front stays until you leave it and a prompt typed in it after landing keeps it open; one closed without being seen leaves a notification while Notify when autopilot lands is on

label: Autopilot's hands-free mode
description: Lets autopilot's menu offer 'Hands-free', which has its tabs take the recommended option of what they would ask you (a question box, a question that ends the turn, an item whose plan needs a choice), write each decision into the item's plan as a 'Decided hands-free' line, and land without asking; what your rules or a skill say must be asked still asks. The mode itself starts off. Off, the menu doesn't offer it and every tab asks as usual

label: Notify when autopilot lands
description: Puts each item autopilot lands without asking, and each landed tab it closes before you saw it, in the sidebar's notifications and the Slack relay's main DM. Off, they show only in the Autopilot view's Landed column, the Notifications view's history (as dismissed) and the item's Done: line

label: Estimated finish
description: Autopilot's view says when the note's ready items should all be done ("done by about 3:40 PM · 6 left"), from the median time its recent items took from opening to landing, its slots and its tabs still at work, and how many items wait on you (an open choice it won't take, a design board to review). Off, its heading has no estimate

label: Keep opening tabs while I'm away
description: Autopilot keeps opening tabs for the note's next items while you're away (the screen locked, or no input for 10 minutes), up to its slots, most tabs open and spend limit, so it works through the note overnight with a terminal attached. Off, it opens nothing while you're away and finishes only the tabs already open

label: Autopilot's push allowed in auto mode
description: A tab autopilot opens in a repository that lands straight on a branch starts its Claude with the landing's push command, switchboard land-lock push, allowed for that session, so Claude Code's auto mode doesn't refuse it; the command pushes without asking only while the tab's "Land without asking" is on and its checks pass, and every other push still asks, as does the push after your yes, which no rule allows. Off, the session gets no rule of its own, so auto mode judges the command itself and a tab landing without asking may stop at it

label: Routines
description: Prompts of yours on a schedule, each run by a headless Claude allowed only the routine's tools, opening no tab, and the Routines view in mission control; off, no routine runs and the view is gone, the routines kept

label: Ticket board
description: Mission control's Tickets view, which asks Linear about the issues assigned to you every two minutes

label: Inbox
description: Mission control's Inbox view and the sidebar's count of it: your unread Linear mentions, comments and assignments, asked of Linear every two minutes #linear

label: Resources
description: Mission control's Resources view: the computer's CPU and memory, and a table of the CPU and memory each tab's processes use, sorted by CPU or memory, read from the kernel every few seconds only while the view is in front, as a board of sparklines and each tab's process tree, whose menu can end a process. Off, the view and its readings are gone

label: Usage
description: Mission control's Usage view: today's Claude spend and how much of the rate limits is used

label: Requests in Usage
description: The Usage view lists today's requests to services outside this computer (GitHub, Linear, Slack, Anthropic and the rest), by protocol and by service, as Switchboard counts them; off, it leaves them out

label: Keys
description: Mission control's Keys view, which M-/ opens: every key Switchboard binds, the workspace's grouped by their first tag, then the sidebar's, mission control's, M-d's and Notes', then the commands reached only through M-p, with / to filter, Enter's menu to press a workspace key and m's to find a key by pressing it, on a board with a heatmap of the Alt keys you pressed this week (counted with habits on); off, M-/ reaches the pane

label: Diff story progress
description: While M-d's story is told, its cover shows which model is telling it and what it is reading, each page as it names it and the time taken, t showing its answer itself as it comes; off, a spinner alone

label: Diff story told ahead
description: When a tab's branch has a new commit, its M-d story is told in the background, so M-d opens on it at once rather than waiting under its cover; sends that branch's diff and commit messages to Claude (Haiku, or Sonnet for a large change, as "Model that tells the diff's story" picks) for each new commit, a run taking up to five and a half minutes

label: Uncommitted changes in M-d
description: M-d's diff runs from the PR's base to the working tree, marking files with changes not yet committed and listing them in a last page; off, it shows the branch's commits only

label: Diff file list wide
description: M-d's file list opens wide enough for its longest path (at most half the screen), E narrowing it; off, it opens narrow and E widens it

label: Resize the diff's file list
description: A drag of M-d's file list's right edge, lit under the mouse, or the pane resize keys (C-M-S-h and C-M-S-l) while the list has the keys, gives the list a width of its own, from 24 columns to half the diff's width, which every diff opens at after, E going between it and the longest path; the diff's menu (m, or a right click) has "Use the file list's default width". Off, the list takes the width it had before (30 columns, or its longest path with diff_list_wide and E), its edge takes no drag and the pane resize keys move the pane's divider

label: Diff story a page at a time
description: ]p and [p in M-d's diff open the story's pages one at a time, each a diff of its own as if it were a commit, [p from the first going back to the whole diff; off, they do nothing

label: Diff story reads the tab's plan
description: M-d's story, told ahead or on opening, is given the tab's plan note (an autopilot item's plan) as well as the commits, so its pages can say what problem each solves and what was passed over; off, it reads the commits and the diff alone. Sends the plan note's words to Claude (Haiku, which tells every story that reads the plan)

label: Open the diff on what changes
description: M-d tells the diff's story in chapters of pages (the goal's chapter, one for each part it can be read without, and the side work) and opens on what changes: before and after in plain words and how and why for each page, an outline of the chapters and pages beside it. Enter reads down one column, each page's claim, what it decided and instead of what, and its changes, tests folded last; What runs shows the steps in the order they happen. The story's map, a box a page and an arrow to what each builds on, is a third view, and the files stay a view of their own (g s, g m and g f, or m), opening in the view used last, or on the talk while diff_story_talk is on; off, the story is one list of pages over the files. A story already told is told again the first time either way

label: Open the diff as a talk
description: With the story in chapters (diff_story_map), M-d opens on the Talk view, first in the views' switch: the change in one sentence and one worked example taken from its own tests, then the flow that example takes, each step, and the code, a zoom at a time (Gist, Flow, Steps, Code; - and + zoom out and in, the left and right arrows go between slides), the example's value shown at every step. With no test giving one, it says so rather than make one up; off, the Talk view is gone and M-d opens as it did

label: Model that tells the diff's story
description: Which model tells M-d's story: by size, Sonnet for a change of more than 20 files or 1,500 changed lines and Haiku for any other; or always Haiku, or always Sonnet. A story that reads the tab's plan (diff_story_plan) is always told by Haiku, the plan going to Haiku alone. A story keeps the model that told it until the menu's Tell it again

label: Diff story notes on changes
description: M-d's diff shows the story's note over each change worth one, why it is needed, and names the page of a change that belongs to another one than its file; off, only the list's pages

label: M-A cycles idle tabs
description: M-A goes to the next idle tab, in the sidebar's Idle order, wrapping at the end, as M-a walks the tabs that need you; off, M-A reaches the pane

label: Tab history
description: M-h shows a tab's history: its Claude session on a timeline (its state, your turns, commits, review rounds and context) under its screen as it was at the moment you move to, the screens kept in the server's memory only, never on disk, and the rest read from the session's transcript; off, nothing is kept, M-h says it is off and the header has no History key

label: Tab age and stage times
description: Shows how long each tab has been open, as 'opened 1h12m' in the tab header and on mission control's cards, and how long each stage of an autopilot tab took (or has taken so far) on its board; off, none of them is shown, while a landed item's Done line still says how long it took, since the landing writes it

label: Repeat the tab's header at the bottom
description: Every tab with a header draws the same header again under its panes, its keys, History, ⌘ Commands and buttons taking the same clicks, so a program whose actions sit at the bottom, as Claude Code's prompt does, has the tab's state and keys beside it; it takes four more rows from every tab's panes. Notes' own tab, which has no header while the sidebar shows, and a zoomed pane have none there either. Off, the header is only at the top and the panes reach the bottom of the screen

label: Search what panes show
description: M-j's picker (and M-b w) finds a tab by what its panes show as well as by its name: each pane's screen and the last lines of its scrollback (Lines searched in each pane) are read in the server's memory as you type, never written anywhere, and each tab found that way shows its matching lines under its row, the tabs found by name first; its row's menu can go to the match in copy mode. Search everything (M-S-f) finds tabs by what their panes show the same way. Off, the picker and search everything match the tabs' names alone

label: Search tabs' conversations
description: Search everything (M-S-f) finds a tab by what was said in its Claude conversation as well, your prompts and Claude's replies (not its tool calls), read from the session's transcript where Claude Code wrote it on this computer and kept in memory, never sent anywhere; Enter on a tab found that way opens its history (M-h) at the moment it was said. Off, search everything finds tabs by their names and what their panes show alone

label: Lines searched in each pane
description: How far back Search what panes show reads each pane's scrollback, above its screen: 200 lines, 1000, or all the pane keeps

label: Widest a lone pane gets
description: A tab with one pane (or zoomed into one) is drawn at most this wide, against the sidebar, its program given that width and the columns at its right the sidebar's sunken surface with a rule at the pane's right edge; panes stacked one above another (M-J) keep that width; with a split side by side the panes share the whole width and may be wider. Mission control always fills the width. Besides the widths listed, Columns… takes any number from 80 typed in, as `switchboard setting lone_pane_width <n>` does. A drag of the rule at a lone pane's right edge, or the pane resize keys (C-M-S-h and C-M-S-l), gives that tab alone a width of its own, kept through restarts and cleared with M-p's or the tab's menu's "Use the default width", leaving this setting, which every other tab takes, as it is. Off, as it is unless you choose a width, a lone pane fills the width

label: Hints in the side panel
description: The side panel, the columns right of a lone pane narrowed by Widest a lone pane gets, lists, centered in it, what the pane can open, each its key and a click that does what the key does: the tab's note, a split to the right, the PR and the ticket when the tab has one (in Claude's place), and a link read beside the pane, with how to widen the pane under them; nothing shows where they don't fit. Off, the side panel is the plain sunken surface

label: Open views in the side panel
description: With a tab's one pane narrowed by Widest a lone pane gets and at least 80 columns spare at its right, M-d's diff, lazygit, and the PR and ticket views that open in Claude's place open in the side panel instead, the pane keeping its width beside it (the diff and lazygit take Diff's share in the side panel, narrowing the pane while one is open); the same key, q or M-w closes the view and the tab is one narrow pane again. With something already in the side panel, they open in its place, but for the PR view (M-v), which closes what is there and takes its columns, the pane keeping the width it had. With fewer columns spare, they open in its place. Off, they always open in the pane's place

label: Open a tab's ticket, PR or note beside it
description: A new tab whose one pane leaves room in the side panel (Widest a lone pane gets, with Open views in the side panel on) opens the first it has of its PR (the PR view, as M-v opens it), its ticket (the ticket view, as M-i opens it) and its plan or note (Notes, as M-e opens it, with Notes in each tab on), the keys staying in its pane. A PR or ticket found a moment later takes the place of what comes after it in that order; once you close the view or open another pane in the tab, it is left as you set it. Off, a tab opens with the side panel empty

label: Diff's share in the side panel
description: How much of the width beside the sidebar M-d's diff and lazygit take when they open in the side panel: half, two thirds or three quarters, the pane narrowed to the rest while one is open and given its own width back when it closes, or the side panel alone, the pane keeping its width. Where the side panel already gives them more, they take it. Dragging the line between them resizes for that one alone

label: Open boxes in the side panel
description: With a tab's one pane narrowed by Widest a lone pane gets, a box about the tab (its links, pictures and the tabs it mentions, answering its Claude, which note is its, naming or renaming it, its menu and its full title, sending its Claude's last reply on, Work on this item) opens as a pane in the side panel, the empty columns at the pane's right, as tall as they are, the hints there hidden while it is open; every other box, a message and a notification among them, goes in the middle of the screen. With too few columns spare it goes in the middle of the screen too. Off, every box goes in the middle of the screen

label: Show images in the side panel
description: With a tab's one pane narrowed by Widest a lone pane gets, a picture Claude or a skill shows you (switchboard look) is drawn as a pane in the side panel, the empty columns at the pane's right, two or more stacked top to bottom with their names, the hints there hidden while they show; M-Esc or the × closes them (a click on them too, with Choose a picture beside a pane and act on it off; on, a click chooses one), and with more than fit the wheel over them and M-PgDn and M-PgUp page through them. Asked for from a tab not in front, they wait for its side panel until the tab is. With too few columns spare, a split, more than six pictures or a terminal that draws no images, they open in the desktop's viewer, as a video or a PDF always does. Off, they always open in the desktop's viewer

label: Choose a picture beside a pane and act on it
description: With pictures shown in the side panel (switchboard look), each is drawn in a card, the one under the mouse lit, and a click on one (or M-p's Choose a picture shown beside the pane, for the first) chooses it and gives the pictures the keys, the tab's pane greyed: j and k, the arrows and Tab move the choice, paging to keep it in view, Enter, Space or a right click open its menu (Open in Finder, Open in Preview, Copy its path, Close the pictures), Esc gives the keys back to the tab with the pictures still up, and M-Esc or the × closes them. Off, the pictures take no keys and a click on them closes them

label: M-{ and M-} go back and forward
description: M-{ and M-} go back and forward through the tabs and mission control views you visited, as a browser's back and forward do, and do nothing with nowhere further to go, the ← and → buttons before mission control's ⊞ do the same, and M-Tab goes to the tab or view before; off, they go to the tab on the left and right, as the prefix's p and n always do, the buttons are left out, and M-Tab goes to the tab before

label: How long to wait for the next digit of a tab's number
description: After M-1 to M-9, how long a digit typed next is taken for the tab's number rather than the pane, so M-1 then 6 goes to tab 16; each digit starts the wait again while an open tab's number could still grow from it, and the tab the digits name comes once it passes or another key is pressed. With no open tab past 9 whose number starts with the digit, nothing waits

label: Leave tabs you pass through out of the history
description: A tab or mission control view in front under a second, passed through on the way somewhere (stepping through the tabs, the sidebar's cursor, M-a through several), isn't a step for M-{ and M-}, and M-Tab goes to the place before it; off, every tab and view left is a step

label: One Claude to a tab
description: A Claude session started in a tab already running one moves to a tab of its own, since the sidebar, the Slack relay, M-c and the PR view's /resolve-conflicts each take a tab's Claude to be one pane

label: Name new tabs
description: M-t and M-n ask what to call the tab they open: a name typed in, its ticket and the ticket's title, or shaping a ticket, each optional; off, the tab is named after its directory

label: Opening-link message
description: Opening a link says where it is going (the site, Chrome and its profile) in a box until the browser comes to the front, since a profile's Chrome can take seconds to start. Off, links open with nothing said

label: Calendar changes
description: In the sidebar's notifications, what changed on today's calendar since you last looked at it: an event added, moved, renamed or gone; looking at the Calendar view clears them

label: Resize Notes' list and plan by dragging or the pane resize keys
description: A drag of the line right of Notes' list of notes, or the pane resize keys (C-M-S-h and C-M-S-l) while the list has the keys, gives the list a width of its own, from 30 columns to half of Notes, kept through restarts; "Use the default width" in Notes' palette, or a double click on the edge, goes back to the width the screen gives it. The plan beside a note resizes the same way by the line at its left, while the plan has the keys, keeping the note at least 24 columns. Off, the list and the plan keep the widths the screen gives them, their edges take no drag and the pane resize keys move the pane's divider as they did before

label: A Notes app in each tab
description: M-e opens a Notes app beside the pane in the tab you're in, on that tab's note, and every other tab keeps its own open; a note open in one tab shows read-only in another, naming the tab that has it, until that tab's app lets it go. Off, there is one Notes, which M-e moves between the tabs

label: Hide the sidebar beside a tab
description: When M-e brings Notes beside another tab's pane, put the notes app's sidebar away so the note has the room, and show it again in Notes' own tab

label: Notes command palette
description: M-p with Notes in front lists every command Notes has, each with its key, ahead of the workspace's, as Ctrl-Shift-P does in Notes run alone; off, M-p leaves them out and Ctrl-Shift-P in Notes run alone says the palette is off

label: Preview a note read-only
description: M-p's "Preview a note…" and Notes' "Preview this note" show a note read-only in the pane's place, drawn as GitHub draws Markdown and following the note as it changes, until q, Esc or the command again gives the pane back; off, both commands are gone

label: Ctrl-V pastes an image
description: Ctrl-V while typing in a note pastes the clipboard's image under the line, as in Claude Code, when the clipboard holds one; off, or with no image there, Ctrl-V types the next key as it is, as in Vim

label: Images drawn in a note
description: An image pasted into a note (Format menu, Paste image) drawn under the line that names it, in a terminal that speaks the kitty graphics protocol (Ghostty and kitty do), or one that gets sixel by Image protocol (Windows Terminal, by default); off, it is its name, which Enter opens as "Enter shows a picture full size" says

label: Draw Mermaid diagrams
description: A ```mermaid block in a note (a flowchart, its subgraphs among it, or a sequence diagram) drawn as its diagram while the cursor is outside it, and as its code while the cursor is in it; the Format menu's Show diagram code shows a note's blocks as code until Show diagrams. Off, every block shows as its code

label: Recent notes in the sidebar
description: Notes' sidebar shows the notes you opened last under Recent, above the folders. Off, the sidebar shows only the folders.

label: Relative line numbers
description: Notes numbers each line by its distance from the cursor's line, the cursor's line showing its own number, as Vim's relativenumber, for jumps like 5j. Off, every line shows its own number.

label: Chips on checklist items
description: Each checklist item shows chips: the tab working on it (its number in the tab's color, a click going there), "landed <hash>" once ticked with its commit named under it, "plan" where it links its plan (a click opening it), "needs a choice" while one waits and "chose" once made; with a Plan: line under the item they are drawn in that line's place, its text shown while the cursor is on it, else at the item's right, its text cut with … before them except on the cursor's line; off, items are their text alone

label: Enter shows a picture full size
description: Enter or a click on a note's picture shows it full size over the notes pane, as it does a picture or diagram under the cursor in the PR, ticket, link and file views, drawn by the workspace in a terminal that speaks the kitty graphics protocol (Ghostty, kitty), or as sixel where Image protocol gives a terminal sixel (Windows Terminal, by default), with "Images in the workspace" on, Esc going back; off, or where the terminal can't, it opens in Quick Look or the desktop's image viewer

label: Toolbar
description: A row of buttons over each note, one for each of the Format menu's styles (bold, italic, headings, lists, checklist, table, link, image) and ⋯ for the whole menu, each acting on the line or the selection; off, the Format menu is Ctrl-P alone

label: Tell a note's new tab its note
description: A new tab opened for a note from Notes starts Claude knowing the note's title and file (added to its system prompt, no turn spent), to read when you ask, or first while Point Claude at the tab's note is on; off, it starts as any other tab

label: wtpr asks where the PR stands
description: Claude, started in a PR's worktree by wtpr (or mission control's "work on it in a new tab"), first reads the PR, its review threads, failing checks and ticket and says where it stands and what it would do next, changing nothing until you say; off, it starts with no prompt

label: Notes beside a note's tab
description: Opening a note's tab from Notes (t, or M-p's Open the tab for the note) moves Notes beside the tab's Claude showing the note, as M-e does; off, it only goes to the tab

label: Show a note's item whole in wt's list
description: M-p's "Start work on a note's checklist items" (M-I) and wt's own list of a note's items show the item under the cursor whole in the lower half of its list, its full text and what is indented under it, since each list cuts an item to one line; off, the list has the whole box

label: Ask for a tab's note
description: When M-e brings Notes beside a tab with no note of its own yet, ask which note is the tab's, a few likely ones and then every note newest first, and show that note beside it from then on

label: M-e opens the tab's plan or autopilot's note
description: M-e shows the note you linked to the tab, else the plan of an autopilot tab's item, else, on an autopilot tab, the note autopilot is working through, else the note shown there last. Off, M-e shows the tab's note or the one shown there last, as before.

label: Point Claude at the tab's note
description: As a Claude session starts in a tab with a note of its own, tell it the note's path and to read it before its first reply, so the note's standing rules reach every session in the tab, in any repository, while Switchboard loads as a plugin (claude_plugin), whose session-start hook does it; off, a session reads the note only when asked to. Off by default, since it has Claude read a note on its own

label: PRs and tickets in tab names
description: Look up each tab's PR number on GitHub and its ticket's title on Linear, or its GitHub issue's title, in the background

label: Follow every PR a tab's session opens
description: A tab follows each pull request its Claude opens or looks at (gh pr create or view), from any branch or repository, as well as its branch's: its label leads with the current one, the sidebar and its Tabs card list each with where it stands, and "Show another of this tab's PRs" makes another current for M-v and M-d. A merged or closed one leaves the list once you have looked at the tab, but a merged one it made stays current while the tab is in that PR's repository, on its branch or on the default branch with no other PR it made open. Off, a tab has only its branch's PR

label: Project colors
description: A color of its own for each project's tab, made from its directory; off, every tab is gray

label: Tab colors
description: The colors tabs take from their project, in the sidebar, the header and Claude's statusline: soft pastels, as the UX 2.0 canvas draws them, or the stronger colors from before. Each tab keeps its own hue either way

label: A color a tab
description: Each tab gets the hue farthest from the open tabs' as it opens, a deeper shade of it when it is close to one, kept while it is open and through restarts, so tabs, and the Usage view's spend chart, tell apart. Off, a tab wears its directory's color, the same for every tab of one checkout

label: Folder for new tabs instead of home
description: A new tab, or a split, that would start in your home folder starts in this folder instead, as does the first tab when the workspace starts, while it is a folder: Claude Code asks whether to trust the home folder every time a session starts there, and a folder here is asked about once. A tab opened from a pane in another folder keeps that folder. Home, the default, starts them at home

label: Images in the workspace
description: Draws avatars, pictures, meters, charts and the shadow under boxes as images where the terminal can show them: by kitty's graphics protocol (Ghostty, kitty), or as sixel where Image protocol gives a terminal sixel (Windows Terminal, by default), the shadow there staying half blocks, since a sixel can't sit under text. Off, they are drawn with characters

label: Scroll bars
description: A scroll bar at the right of every list, view and pane with more than fits, showing where you are: a click on its track pages toward the click, and dragging its thumb scrolls with it. Off, nothing is drawn there

label: People's photos
description: Avatars show people's photos from Slack (through the Slack relay's app, with the users:read scope), Linear and GitHub, and, with calendar_photos on, calendar attendees' by their address, each fetched once and kept in ~/.cache/switchboard/photos for 30 days. Off, nothing is fetched and an avatar is the person's initial

label: Pictures and diagrams in the views
description: Draws the pictures on lines of their own and the Mermaid diagrams in the PR, ticket, link and file views as images where the terminal can show them (Ghostty, kitty, or as sixel where Image protocol gives a terminal sixel, Windows Terminal by default), fetching the pictures and drawing the diagrams with Mermaid in Chrome, and draws the diagrams of the description beside mission control's PR and ticket boards the same way (with "Images in the workspace" on too). Off, a picture is its name and a diagram is drawn with characters

label: A cursor in the views
description: Gives the PR, ticket, link and file views a cursor, a yellow › that j and k move from line to line, a picture or diagram one step, the screen scrolling to keep it in sight; Enter or a click on a picture or diagram shows it full size over the view, as a note's does, Esc going back. Off, the views scroll as less does, and a click on a picture opens its link

label: Theme
description: The header's, the pane borders' and the boxes' colors, dark drawn in the UX 2.0 canvas's colors on a terminal that shows truecolor and in the 256-color palette elsewhere; system follows the terminal's own background, which it is asked for as it attaches

label: Set the terminal's colors
description: While Switchboard is attached, sets your terminal's background and text colors to the dark theme's, so the padding around the window matches; puts the terminal's own back when you detach. Off, the terminal keeps its own colors.

label: Image protocol
description: How pictures (a note's images, the PR and ticket image views, the pictures and diagrams in the PR, ticket, link and file views, and the workspace's own: avatars, meters, charts, switches, the diagrams beside a board, a picture shown full size), and the rounded ends of its pills, reach your terminal: auto picks by the terminal, kitty's graphics protocol for Ghostty and kitty, sixel for one that says it draws sixel when asked as it attaches (Windows Terminal from 1.22, foot, WezTerm, xterm with sixel, mlterm), and the text forms for any other; kitty sends them by kitty's protocol to every terminal, as chosen, one that doesn't speak it showing boxes in their place; sixel has the workspace draw each picture itself as sixel where it shows for every terminal, as chosen, Ghostty and kitty included, one that doesn't draw sixel showing blanks in their place, the shadow under a box drawn with characters. Notes, the image view and the PR, ticket, link and file views opened after a change draw by it

label: Copy Claude's reply
description: M-y copies the latest reply of the tab's Claude to the clipboard, read from its session transcript; off, the key reaches the pane

label: Programs in panes copy
description: A program in the pane in front of you can put text on the clipboard (OSC 52), as Claude Code's /copy and Neovim do; one in a pane you aren't looking at never can. Off, every pane's copy is ignored, and only Switchboard's own copies (copy mode, M-y) reach the clipboard

label: Log Claude's hooks
description: Write a line to the server's log (server.log in Switchboard's state directory) for each hook Claude Code runs in a pane: the event, the tool, the pane, the call's id, the subagent and a notification's kind, never what was asked or run; for finding out why a tab showed the wrong state. Off, nothing is logged

label: Show a tab's full title
description: M-p's "Show this tab's full title", the sidebar's i and a tab's menu in mission control (and M-T, with "M-T reopens the last closed tab" off) show the tab's whole title in a box, with its branch, directory, PR and ticket, which the sidebar and the header cut; off, M-T reaches the pane

label: M-T reopens the last closed tab
description: M-T reopens the tab closed most recently, in its directory with its Claude resumed; pressed again, the one before. Off, M-T shows the tab's full title as before

label: Save what panes show
description: Keep each pane's screen in the layout saves, to show again after a restart, and a closed tab's last screen for the Reopen view; it can hold secrets

label: Offer to apply a landed change
description: After queue-and-clean lands work, it lists what the change needs to take effect (Switchboard built and put in place, the Slack relay restarted, an install, a migration) and offers to do it

label: Restore on start
description: Bring back the last saved tabs and panes, each Claude resumed, when the server starts with none open

label: Load Switchboard as a plugin
description: Claude in Switchboard's panes loads its hooks (the tabs' Claude states), skills and instructions as a plugin, and setup keeps them out of ~/.claude, so Claude elsewhere has only your own; it needs Claude Code 2.1.280 or later, and managed settings that don't set disableSideloadFlags; a managed plugin that answers Claude Code's settings before Switchboard's leaves its panes without Switchboard's statusline, which Switchboard says when it happens. Off, setup puts them in ~/.claude as before, for every Claude of yours. Changing it moves them over

label: Context in Claude's status line
description: Claude Code's status line under its prompt says how full the context is, beside the model, inside the workspace as outside it. Off, with mission control's Usage view on, the status line inside the workspace shows the model alone and the Usage view's Sessions show the context; without it, it shows the context anyway

label: Switchboard's statusline in its panes
description: With Switchboard loaded as a plugin, Claude in its panes draws Switchboard's statusline, which keeps each session's context and spend for mission control's Usage view, and your own statusline is drawn everywhere else; nothing is written to your Claude Code settings either way. Off, the plugin leaves the statusline alone, so a Claude started in a pane after the change draws yours too, and that view gets nothing from it

label: Switchboard's permissions in its panes
description: With Switchboard loaded as a plugin, Claude in its panes runs the few of Switchboard's own commands its instructions name (switchboard tabs, show, set and the like) without asking, unless a rule of yours says otherwise, and is refused reading .env files and running git pull; nothing is written to your Claude Code settings either way. Its skills allow their own commands themselves, whatever this says. Off, a Claude started in a pane after the change asks for those commands as for any other, and refuses nothing for Switchboard

label: Queue heavy work
description: cargo, npm and pnpm run in a pane put builds, test runs and package installs through a queue, so only as many of each kind go at once as the caps below say, and the cores are shared out between them (CARGO_BUILD_JOBS, RUST_TEST_THREADS); a command waiting says "Waiting for a build slot (2nd in line)", and a slot is let go as its command ends or is killed. Off, every command runs at once, as the real program would

label: Builds at once
description: How many compiles (cargo build, check, clippy, doc, and the compile half of cargo test) go at once across every pane while Queue heavy work is on; auto is a quarter of the cores. Off, compiles don't wait

label: Test runs at once
description: How many test runs (the run half of cargo test, cargo nextest run) go at once across every pane while Queue heavy work is on, each given the cores shared out. Off, test runs don't wait

label: Package builds at once
description: How many npm ci, npm install, npm run build, pnpm install and pnpm build go at once across every pane while Queue heavy work is on. Off, they don't wait

label: Rules in reviews
description: codex-review gives the reviewer the repository's CLAUDE.md and AGENTS.md as the base has them and your own ~/.claude/CLAUDE.md with what it imports, and reports a change that breaks one; off, it reviews without them, and your rules aren't sent to the reviewer

label: Land without asking
description: Each tab /wt, wtb or autopilot opens is marked to land without asking (@land), and follows the setting as it changes, a tab's own menu deciding for it meanwhile: queue-and-clean opens its PR with no question once two review rounds of the change came back clean (the PR's CI then running its tests), or pushes its landing once its tests pass too, a push a CLAUDE.md says to ask about (a release's version bump) still asking, and once its PR merges it skips the deploy-test approval where the repository has no deploy or test to wait for; off, it asks before its first push and for that approval

label: Learn from what you pick
description: M-p remembers what you typed before each pick, and puts that command first when you type the same again

label: Links you gave Claude
description: M-p's link commands also list the links in what you sent the pane's Claude, pasted text included, which Claude Code doesn't show. Off, they list only what the pane shows

label: Pictures and videos Claude named
description: M-p's "Open an image or video from this pane" also lists the files the last turns of the tab's Claude named that the screen doesn't show, read from its transcript. Off, it lists only what the pane and the tab's note show

label: Pane commands read the tab's note
description: M-p's link, picture and mentioned-tab commands also read the note open in the tab (M-e): from Claude's pane its links, files and tabs after the pane's, and from the notes pane the tab's other panes' after the note's. Off, each reads only the pane it runs from

label: Commands button
description: A ⌘ Commands button that opens M-p when clicked: at the right end of the tab header's keys, where a click while the palette is open closes it, and on the notes list's top line in Notes' own tab, which has no header

label: Security review in the review loop
description: /review-loop runs Claude Code's /security-review on the branch once before its first round, its findings fixed or asked about as the rounds' are

label: Review loop takes its recommended choice without asking
description: /review-loop settles each medium finding, and each low a confirmation round finds, as it would recommend, fixing it or leaving it as a known gap, and lists each in its final report with what it did and why, so you can overturn one there; off, it asks about each with Fix it or Leave it, its recommendation first

label: Review from three angles at once
description: Each round of codex-review on a branch runs three reviewers at once, one looking hardest at failure paths, one at the skills, docs, settings and callers the change touches, one at the change against its claims, their findings merged into the round's one answer, which is clean only when all three find nothing; off, a round runs one reviewer with no focus

label: Ask before closing a pane
description: M-w asks first when a program runs in the pane it closes (a shell at its prompt closes at once), and before closing a tab from its Claude pane, its one pane or its sidebar row; off, it closes the pane or tab at once whatever runs in it

label: M-w closes the tab from Claude or a lone pane
description: M-w in a tab's Claude pane, in a tab's one pane, or on its sidebar row, asks to close the tab, and anywhere else closes only the pane; off, M-w closes the pane it is pressed in and the last pane closes its tab

label: Tips
description: A box in the top-right corner, once each, when a key would help (M-a, M-j, putting a pane back); any key closes it

label: Suggestions from how you work
description: Count the keys you press, the commands you pick in M-p and the mission control views you open, on this computer only and never sent anywhere, and suggest in the notifications a view to turn off that you never open, a key for a command you keep picking in M-p, or a feature that is off which what you do would use; off, what was counted is removed

label: Easy mode
description: Keys for people who don't know Vim's, in Notes and M-d's diff: Shift-arrows and the mouse select, typing replaces a selection, Cmd-S saves, Cmd-Z undoes, Cmd-Shift-Z redoes and Cmd-X cuts in a note (where the terminal sends them as the guide says), and the diff gets a row of buttons for its keys; mission control's boxes, the update box's and M-w's menus, messages, tips, and Notes' Format menu, palette and finder get a × in their top-right corner that a click or Tab and Enter closes, with Click in menus on (lists to pick from, such as M-p's, keep Esc alone); Vim's keys keep working. Takes effect when Notes or the diff next opens

label: Key help line
description: With Easy mode on, a line at the bottom of Notes and M-d's diff naming the keys that work there

label: Alt-arrows move between panes
description: M-Left, M-Right, M-Up and M-Down move to the pane on that side, as C-w h, l, k and j do in Vim; off, they reach the pane

label: Resize the pane beside a board
description: In mission control, the pane resize keys (C-M-S-h and C-M-S-l) and a drag of its left edge widen or narrow the pane beside the PRs, Tickets and Autopilot boards, each board keeping its width. Off, the pane keeps its share of the screen and the keys and its edge do nothing there

label: C-w then h, j, k or l moves between panes
description: C-w followed by h, j, k or l moves to the pane on that side, as in Vim, which itself still gets C-w; C-w twice sends one to the pane. In mission control, C-w and h or l move between a view's left panel, list and the pane beside it, and C-w and j or k to the next or last section a view stacks in its list. Off, C-w reaches the pane as it is, deleting a word in a shell or Claude's prompt, and a mission control view's list keeps the keys

label: Extended keys
description: Your terminal is asked to tell keys such as Ctrl-Shift-P from Ctrl-P and Shift-Enter from Enter, as tmux's extended-keys did, and a program that asks for them (Notes, Neovim, the kitty keyboard protocol's) gets them so, while the rest get the keys as before; off, every key reaches every program as a plain terminal sends it. Takes effect when a terminal next attaches and for panes opened after

label: Update check
description: Offer a new release of Switchboard: when a terminal attaches and every hour, only when one attaches, or never

label: Offer to restart after an update
description: Once switchboard update has put a new release in place, ask whether to restart the workspace on it now, keeping every tab and what runs in it; off, it only says how (switchboard upgrade)

label: Your files from a git repository
description: Your own files (settings.json, keys.json, sidebar.json and the rest of ~/.config/switchboard) are read from and written to a clone of the git repository files.json names (Settings' Your files' repository), in ~/.local/share/switchboard/files: pulled as Switchboard starts and every ten minutes, and each change committed and pushed at once, after leak-check has read it and asked about anything it found. files.json, trusted-dirs, repos.json, sidebar-plugins, slack-relay.json, linear.json, oncall.json, oncall-rules.md, slack-updates.json, autopilot-claim.json, secrets.json and leak-check.txt stay on this computer, as this setting does. Off, files.json is ignored and your files are the ones in ~/.config/switchboard

label: Slack relay
description: Mission control's Slack relay view: whether the relay is running, what it sent today, and which kinds of message reach you and how, with presets. Off, the view is gone and the relay's settings stay in Settings

label: Haiku summaries
description: One line on what each tab is doing in the relay's Home tab and progress, each a paid Haiku call

label: Ask before typing over a draft
description: A message sent to a tab from Slack while text is typed and unsent in its prompt waits, and the thread asks whether to replace the draft, send after it or keep it. Off, the message is typed after whatever is there and sent, as before

label: Close the relay's tab when it stops
description: Stopping the Slack relay, from M-p, `slack-relay stop`, `stop` in its DM or Ctrl-C in its tab, closes its tab; a crash or a start it refuses keeps the tab at a shell with the error. Off, the tab stays at a shell whenever the relay ends

label: Reminder tabs on the Slack Home
description: Lists the tabs under the sidebar's Reminders on the Slack app's Home too, each saying when it reminds you. Off, they are left out until their reminder comes due, and the Home says how many

label: Notes in Slack
description: Lets the Slack app's Autopilot form name your notes, so you can pick the note it works from Slack, and the Home tab's autopilot section name the note it works; only the notes' names are sent, never their items. Off, the form names no note and starts autopilot on the note it last worked, and the Home tab says "your note"

label: Autopilot in Slack
description: While autopilot works, the Slack app's Home tab shows its progress above Needs you: paused or not, when its ready items should be done, how many items stand in each column of its board, today's spend against its limit, its tabs in flight with a link to each one's thread, and Pause, Resume and Settings buttons. It is edited in place at most once a minute, and nothing new is posted for it. Off, the Home tab leaves autopilot out

label: Prompts and questions
description: A permission prompt, a question or a wait, with buttons that answer it. Notify me puts it in the tab's thread with a line there mentioning you, which is what Slack notifies you for; Thread only puts it in the thread alone. It can't be turned off, since only Slack may be there to answer it. The tab's thread keeps a record only of what is sent.

label: Dialogs before a session starts
description: A trust or sign-in dialog Claude Code shows before its session starts. Notify me puts it in the tab's thread with a line there mentioning you; Thread only in the thread alone. It can't be turned off, since only Slack may be there to answer it. The tab's thread keeps a record only of what is sent.

label: Finished turns
description: Claude's last message of each turn. Notify me puts it in the tab's thread with a line there mentioning you; Thread only in the thread alone; Don't send leaves it in the tab. A turn that answers a message you sent the tab from Slack always reaches you where you asked, whatever this says. The tab's thread keeps a record only of what is sent.

label: Turns another tab or a task started
description: Posts a tab's finished turn in its thread when another tab's message or a background task started it, or when it wrote no reply. Off, only turns you started that wrote a reply, and tabs waiting on you, are posted

label: Tabs that may be stuck
description: A tab marked working that has gone quiet. Notify me puts it in the tab's thread with a line there mentioning you; Thread only in the thread alone; Don't send leaves it unsaid. The tab's thread keeps a record only of what is sent.

label: Commits, pushes and pull requests
description: Each commit, push and pull request a tab makes. Notify me puts it in the tab's thread with a line there mentioning you; Thread only in the thread alone; Don't send leaves it unsaid. The tab's thread keeps a record only of what is sent.

label: Failed commits, pushes and pull requests
description: A commit, push or pull request that failed, with the reason. Notify me puts it in the tab's thread with a line there mentioning you; Thread only in the thread alone; Don't send leaves it unsaid. The tab's thread keeps a record only of what is sent.

label: Full context
description: A tab past 90% of its context, with a button to compact it. Notify me puts it in the tab's thread with a line there mentioning you; Thread only in the thread alone; Don't send leaves it unsaid. The tab's thread keeps a record only of what is sent.

label: Notices from other programs
description: What `switchboard slack-relay notify` sends, such as a landing or an on-call alert, as a message of its own in the main DM, which Slack notifies you for. Don't send refuses them, and the program that sent one is told it wasn't sent

label: Autopilot's tabs
description: What the relay sends about a tab autopilot opened. Like any tab follows the settings above; Landings and failures only sends only its prompts, dialogs and failed commits, pushes and pull requests, each as its own setting says, and leaves out its finished turns, stuck notes, commits, pushes, pull requests and full context

label: Quiet hours
description: Between Quiet hours from and to, by this computer's clock, what would notify you goes to its tab's thread only, but for prompts and dialogs while "Prompts notify in quiet hours" is on. Offline and crash messages, and answers to what you sent from Slack, still notify. Off, the relay notifies at any hour

label: Quiet hours from
description: When quiet hours start each day, while Quiet hours is on

label: Quiet hours to
description: When quiet hours end each day, while Quiet hours is on

label: Prompts notify in quiet hours
description: Prompts, questions and dialogs still notify you during quiet hours. Off, during quiet hours they go to their tab's thread alone, with no line mentioning you, as the other kinds do

label: Phone app
description: switchboard phone (M-p's "Open the phone app in its own tab") serves a web app on your tailnet alone, for answering, messaging, reminding you of, pinning and closing your Claude tabs (closing asked first, and off with Close tabs from the phone) from the phones phone.json lists: their prompts, their recent turns, and a Web Push naming the tab when one starts waiting on you or its reminder comes due, which passes through your phone's push service. Needs Tailscale. Off, it refuses to start, and one running stops answering

label: Close tabs from the phone
description: A long press on a tab in the phone app's drawer offers Close tab, which asks first and then closes the tab, its Claude and its other panes, written in the server's log. Off, the menu offers no Close tab and the server refuses a close from the phone

label: Buzz the phone
description: The phone app gives a short buzz as you answer a prompt, send a message, open a tab's menu with a long press and swipe far enough to open the drawer, a vibration on Android and a haptic tick on an iPhone with iOS 18 or later. Off, the app never buzzes

label: Coordinator
description: A Claude Code session of its own, outside every tab, that keeps your work moving: woken only by events (a tab's PR merged, a tab finished or waits on you, its note changed, a message from you or another tab), it closes tabs whose PR merged, opens the next ready issues from its note one at a time, keeps its note and files issues after a leak-check. M-C shows it beside the tab in front. It sends its note's contents and your tabs' names to Claude, so it is off by default; off, nothing of it runs

label: Coordinator's model
description: The model the coordinator's session runs on (claude --model), taken up the next time it starts

label: Model that shapes work for the coordinator
description: The model of the subagent the coordinator hands shaping to (/shape): it reads the code, finds the cause and drafts the issue, and the coordinator asks you its questions and files the draft after your yes

label: Coordination note
description: The note the coordinator keeps, with In flight, Next and Deferred sections, by its title in your notes folder; it offers to make it when it isn't there. Besides Coordination, Note… takes any note's title typed in

label: Show the pictures a tab's Claude shows on the phone
description: While the phone app is on, each switchboard look of pictures (a PNG, JPEG, GIF or WebP, up to 20 MB) in a tab running Claude copies them into the phone app's images folder, readable only by you and removed after 30 days, and adds a message holding them to the tab's channel on the phone, each shown whole on a tap. The pictures stay on your computer and your phone on your tailnet. Off, look copies nothing and the channel shows no such message

label: Review before pushing
description: In Switchboard's own repository, a push to main needs a clean /review-loop first (.githooks/pre-push); off, it pushes without one

label: Skills and instructions from the clone
description: A build made from a clone reads its skills, Claude settings, instructions and settings list from that clone's assets/ folder, so a change there is live once it lands: the plugin and the parts you set up are brought up to date within seconds, with no rebuild or restart. A release build has no clone and keeps what it carries. Off, every build uses what it carries

label: Build before restarting
description: M-p's "Restart Switchboard on the latest main" first brings the main clone of the checkout a build from a clone came from up to date with origin, on its default branch with nothing uncommitted, and builds it (cargo build --release --locked; a try builds its worktree) and puts it in place of the binary the server runs, restarting only when that is new (from a cargo target directory, which other worktrees write over, the build goes to ~/.local/bin/switchboard, else a copy in ~/.cache/switchboard/build, and the restart runs from there); off, it restarts on the binary on disk as it is, when that is new

label: Say when main is ahead of this build
description: When Switchboard's main has commits on its default branch that the running build lacks, a notification says how many landings the build lacks, counted (after fetching origin's default branch into the main clone, while GitHub is on) as the server starts, after each landing or merge queue merge and every hour, and its menu restarts on the latest main; off, nothing is counted or shown

label: Start a worktree's build from the main clone's
description: A worktree wt, wtb or wtpr makes starts with its target/ as a copy-on-write clone of the main clone's (APFS on macOS, Btrfs or XFS on Linux), made in the background, so cargo reuses the dependencies the main clone compiled (a dependency with a build script, such as one compiling C, and those built on it build again, since build scripts and their output aren't cloned) and the copy takes no disk space until a build changes it; a worktree holding someone else's code, one on another volume and a filesystem that can't clone get none. Off (the default until it has been tried on real worktrees), a new worktree starts with no build output and compiles everything itself
